new_statements.quote: Sejauh pengamatan, ton dan panjang pendek bunyi dalam bahasa Kalabra tidak fonemik. Unsur suprasegmental yang jelas hanyalah tekanan. Berhubung belum adanya data yang dapat menunjukkan lingkungan yang identik dan analogis, untuk sementara tekanan ini dianggap tidak fonemik. Dan munculnya tekanan ini tidak dapat diramalkan. Tekanan kadang-kadang jatuh pada suku yang pertama, kadang-kadang pada suku yang kedua. Pada kata yang bersuku tiga pada umumnya tekanan jatuh pada suku yang kedua. Contoh: /ɔ'nɔhɔf/ 'yang mana?' /blin'flɔmE/ 'pohon nipa' /tɔ'tbaran/ 'terlentang'
new_statements.translation: As far as observed, tone and length of sounds in Kalabra are not phonemic. The only clear suprasegmental element is stress. Since there are as yet no data that can show identical and analogous environments, this stress is for the time being regarded as non-phonemic. And the occurrence of this stress cannot be predicted. Stress sometimes falls on the first syllable, sometimes on the second. In words of three syllables stress generally falls on the second syllable. Examples: /ɔ'nɔhɔf/ 'which one?', /blin'flɔmE/ 'nipa palm', /tɔ'tbaran/ 'lying on one's back'.

Book p. 31 (PDF 44) ends with the heading '2.10 Unsur Suprasegmental' and the line 'Sejauh pengamatan, ton dan panjang pendek bunyi dalam bahasa Kalabra'; book p. 32 (PDF 45) continues 'tidak fonemik. Unsur suprasegmental yang jelas hanyalah tekanan. Berhubung belum adanya data yang dapat menunjukkan lingkungan yang identik dan analogis, untuk sementara tekanan ini dianggap tidak fonemik. Dan munculnya tekanan ini tidak dapat diramalkan. Tekanan kadang-kadang jatuh pada suku yang pertama, kadang-kadang pada suku yang kedua. Pada kata yang bersuku tiga pada umumnya…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is the only clear suprasegmental (no tone, no contrastive length). Its position is described as unpredictable: on the first or the second syllable of disyllables, and usually on the second syllable (= penult) of trisyllables. The authors provisionally call it non-phonemic because they found no minimal or analogous pairs; the source therefore reads as 'unpredictable but non-contrastive' rather than lexically contrastive.
new_statements.exceptions: p. 35 (sec. 3.2 note): in disyllabic words of the shapes KKV.KKV and V.KKVK stress falls on the first syllable (/'tn.sya/, /'a.blil/, which cannot be resyllabified). The dialect word list pp. 5-7 marks stress on both first and second syllables (/'sifko/ 'eye', /ku'dus/ 'bone', /ta'rit/ 'foot', /to'don/ 'night').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation forms of isolated words (phonemic transcription with ' before the stressed syllable); wordlist-based description of the Wanurian (Beraur) dialect; no phrase-level or instrumental data.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes the central Kalabra dialect ('bahasa Kalabra saja') as spoken at Wanurian, the seat of Kecamatan Beraur (data from Wanurian; sec. 1.6, 1.8 of Purba et al. 1987), i.e. language-level kala1256. The authors distinguish a second dialect 'Kalabra Salmit' close to Tehit; Berry & Berry 1987 (WILC 4, p. 44) reassign Salmit to Tehit (tehi1237). Glottolog dates the phonology 1983 (research year 1982/83) and omits the third author; the printed book is dated 1987 with authors Purba, Animung & Lamera (OCLC 20741271).

new_statements.quote: Sejauh pengamatan, ton dan panjang pendek bunyi dalam bahasa Kalabra tidak fonemik. Unsur suprasegmental yang jelas hanyalah tekanan. Berhubung belum adanya data yang dapat menunjukkan lingkungan yang identik dan analogis, untuk sementara tekanan ini dianggap tidak fonemik. Dan munculnya tekanan ini tidak dapat diramalkan. Tekanan kadang-kadang jatuh pada suku yang pertama, kadang-kadang pada suku yang kedua. Pada kata yang bersuku tiga pada umumnya tekanan jatuh pada suku yang kedua. Contoh: /ɔ'nɔhɔf/ 'yang mana?' /blin'flɔmE/ 'pohon nipa' /tɔ'tbaran/ 'terlentang'
new_statements.translation: As far as observed, tone and vowel length in Kalabra are not phonemic. The only clear suprasegmental element is stress. Since there are as yet no data that can show identical and analogous environments, stress is provisionally regarded as non-phonemic. And the occurrence of this stress cannot be predicted. Stress sometimes falls on the first syllable, sometimes on the second. In trisyllabic words stress generally falls on the second syllable. Examples: /ɔ'nɔhɔf/ 'which?', /blin'flɔmE/ 'nipa palm', /tɔ'tbaran/ 'lying on one's back'.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: 6, 47, 48, 51 as images. Title page (PDF p. 6): 'Struktur Bahasa Kalabra (Fonologi), Oleh Theodorus T. Purba, Lisidius Animung, John Lamera, Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Jakarta 1987' - so the reader's 'wrong-item' call is right: this is a second scan of the 1987 phonology, not the 1984 morphology volume. DAFTAR ISI (PDF pp. 12-13) lists 2.10 Unsur Suprasegmental p. 31, 3.2 Distribusi Suku Kata p. 33, 5.3 Kesimpulan p. 63, Lampiran I Tinjauan Tatabahasa p. 68, Lampiran II wordlist p. 81. The quotation is on the page images exactly as given: PDF p. 47 (book p. 31) ends '2.10 Unsur Suprasegmental / Sejauh pengamatan, ton dan panjang pendek bunyi dalam bahasa Kalabra' and PDF p. 48…
new_statements.relation_note: The open copy at the listed URL is NOT the 1984 morphology volume: it is a second (2015 PaperPort, 132-page) scan of Purba, Animung & Lamera 1987, Struktur Bahasa Kalabra (Fonologi), the very book behind the existing catalog statement (title page PDF p. 6; DAFTAR ISI PDF pp. 12-13 identical to the repositori 2476 copy: Bab 1-5 phonology, Lampiran I 'Tinjauan Tatabahasa' pp. 68-80, Lampiran II wordlist pp. 81-116). Its stress statements are word-for-word those already recorded (sec. 2.10 pp. 31-32; 5.3 p. 64), so it agrees with the existing 'lexical (unpredictable)' statement and adds only the p. 35 first-syllable note and the p. 29 unit-phoneme criterion. The 1984 'Morfologi (dan sintaksis)…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is the only clear suprasegmental; the authors call it provisionally non-phonemic (no minimal pairs found) and say its position cannot be predicted: sometimes the first syllable, sometimes the second; in trisyllables usually the second syllable. Tone and length are not phonemic.
new_statements.exceptions: Partial regularity in sec. 3.2 note, p. 35 (PDF p. 51): in disyllables of shape KKV.KKV and V.KKVK the syllabification cannot shift 'karena tekanan jatuh pada suku yang pertama' (/'tn.sya/, /'a.blil/). Sec. 2.9, p. 29 (PDF p. 45): sequences /ky/, /dy/, /tl/ are counted as unit phonemes 'berdasarkan tekanan' ([am'kyan] 'gravel'). Sec. 5.3, p. 64 (PDF p. 80) restates: 'untuk sementara tekanan ini dianggap tidak fonemik dan tidak dapat diramalkan kemunculannya'.
new_statements.identity_note: The 1987 phonology's data come from the central 'Kalabra saja' dialect spoken at Wanurian (Beraur, Kab. Sorong), Tarsa and Buk (sec. 1.6-1.8, pp. 3-7); the second dialect, Kalabra Salmit near Tehit, is only mentioned. The EPrints record 3867 lists only 'Theodorus T. Purba' as author; the title page names Purba, Animung and Lamera.

Nothing missed.
